title: Guidelines for Imaging and Analysis of Reactive Anode Materials Using Electron Microscope
content: Reactive lithium and sodium batteries have step on the stage as promising anode materials due to their high energy density, economic accessibility, and earth abundancy [1, 2]. However, their high chemical reactivity presents significant challenges in characterizing these anode materials and understanding the working mechanisms within the battery system. In recent years, cryogenic techniques, which preserve chemical integrity while maintaining electron beam sensitivity, have enabled the exploration of morphology, elemental distribution, and chemical environment at the solid-liquid interface, therefore, paves a path for performance improvement [3, 4].
